tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

schema.name: Skill
schema.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1 --- 2 title: "Training Overview and Features" 3 layout: single 4 permalink: /training/ 5 toc: true 6 toc_label: "Contents" 7 --- 8 9 # Overview 10 Training advanced deep learning models is challenging. Beyond model design, 11 model scientists also need to set up the state-of-the-art training techniques 12 such as distributed training, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and 13 checkpointing. Yet still, scientists may not achieve the desired system 14 performance and convergence rate. Large model sizes are even more challenging: 15 a large model easily runs out of memory with pure data parallelism and it is 16 difficult to use model parallelism. DeepSpeed addresses these challenges to 17 accelerate model development *and* training. 18 19 ## Distributed, Effective, and Efficient Training with Ease 20 The DeepSpeed API is a lightweight wrapper on [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/). This 21 means that you can use everything you love in PyTorch and without learning a new 22 platform. In addition, DeepSpeed manages all of the boilerplate state-of-the-art 23 training techniques, such as distributed training, mixed precision, gradient 24 accumulation, and checkpoints so that you can focus on your model development. Most 25 importantly, you can leverage the distinctive efficiency and effectiveness benefit of 26 DeepSpeed to boost speed and scale with just a few lines of code changes to your PyTorch 27 models. 28 29 ## Speed 30 DeepSpeed achieves high performance and fast convergence through a combination of 31 efficiency optimizations on compute/communication/memory/IO and effectiveness 32 optimizations on advanced hyperparameter tuning and optimizers. For example: 33 34 * DeepSpeed trains BERT-large to parity in 44 35 mins using 1024 V100 GPUs (64 DGX-2 boxes) and in 2.4 hours using 256 GPUs 36 (16 DGX-2 boxes). 37 38 **BERT-large Training Times** 39 40 | Devices | Source | Training Time | 41 | -------------- | --------- | ---------------------:| 42 | 1024 V100 GPUs | DeepSpeed | **44** min| 43 | 256 V100 GPUs | DeepSpeed | **2.4** hr| 44 | 64 V100 GPUs | DeepSpeed | **8.68** hr| 45 | 16 V100 GPUs | DeepSpeed | **33.22** hr| 46 47 *BERT code and tutorials will be available soon.* 48 49 * DeepSpeed trains GPT2 (1.5 billion parameters) 3.75x faster than state-of-art, NVIDIA 50 Megatron on Azure GPUs. 51 52 *Read more*: [GPT tutorial](/tutorials/megatron/) 53 54 55 56 ## Memory efficiency 57 DeepSpeed provides memory-efficient data parallelism and enables training models without 58 model parallelism. For example, DeepSpeed can train models with up to 13 billion parameters on 59 a single GPU. In comparison, existing frameworks (e.g., 60 PyTorch's Distributed Data Parallel) run out of memory with 1.4 billion parameter models. 61 62 DeepSpeed reduces the training memory footprint through a novel solution called Zero 63 Redundancy Optimizer (ZeRO). Unlike basic data parallelism where memory states are 64 replicated across data-parallel processes, ZeRO partitions model states and gradients to save 65 significant memory. Furthermore, it also reduces activation memory and fragmented memory. 66 The current implementation (ZeRO-2) reduces memory by up to 67 8x relative to the state-of-art. You can read more about ZeRO in our [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054), and 68 in our blog posts related to 69 [ZeRO-1](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/zero-deepspeed-new-system-optimizations-enable-training-models-with-over-100-billion-parameters/) and [ZeRO-2](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/zero-2-deepspeed-shattering-barriers-of-deep-learning-speed-scale/). 70 71 With this impressive memory reduction, early adopters of DeepSpeed have already 72 produced a language model (LM) with over 17B parameters called 73 74 Turing-NLG, 75 establishing a new SOTA in the LM category. 76 77 For model scientists with limited GPU resources, ZeRO-Offload leverages both CPU and GPU memory for training large models. Using a machine with **a single GPU**, our users can run **models of up to 13 billion parameters** without running out of memory, 10x bigger than the existing approaches, while obtaining competitive throughput. This feature democratizes multi-billion-parameter model training and opens the window for many deep learning practitioners to explore bigger and better models. 78 79 ## Scalability 80 DeepSpeed supports efficient data parallelism, model parallelism, pipeline parallelism and their 81 combinations, which we call 3D parallelism. 82 * 3D parallelism of DeepSpeed provides system support to run models with trillions of parameters, read more in our [press-release]({{ site.press_release_v3 }}) and [tutorial](/tutorials/pipeline). 83 * DeepSpeed can run large models more efficiently, up to 10x 84 faster for models with 85 various sizes spanning 1.5B to hundred billion. More specifically, the data parallelism powered by ZeRO 86 is complementary and can be combined with different types of model parallelism. It allows 87 DeepSpeed to fit models using lower degree of model parallelism and higher batch size, offering 88 significant performance gains compared to using model parallelism alone. 89 90 *Read more*: [ZeRO paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054), 91 and [GPT tutorial](/tutorials/megatron). 92 93 ![DeepSpeed Speedup](/assets/images/deepspeed-speedup.png) 94

95 The figure depicts system throughput improvements of DeepSpeed (combining ZeRO-powered data parallelism with model parallelism of NVIDIA Megatron-LM) over using Megatron-LM alone. 96

97 98 ## Communication efficiency 99 Pipeline parallelism of DeepSpeed reduce communication volume during distributed training, which allows users to train multi-billion-parameter models 2–7x faster on clusters with limited network bandwidth. 100 ![Low-bandwidth GPT-2 Performance](/assets/images/pp-lowbw-gpt2.png) 101 102 ## Data efficiency 103 DeepSpeed Data Efficiency Library provides efficient data sampling via curriculum learning and efficient data routing via random layerwise token dropping. The composed solution enables up to 2x data and 2x time saving during GPT-3/BERT pretraining and GPT/ViT finetuning, or further improve model quality under the same data/time. See more in [the tutorial](/tutorials/data-efficiency). 104 105 ## Fast convergence for effectiveness 106 DeepSpeed supports advanced hyperparameter tuning and large batch size 107 optimizers such as [LAMB](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00962). These improve the 108 effectiveness of model training and reduce the number of samples required to 109 convergence to desired accuracy. 110 111 *Read more*: [Tuning tutorial](/tutorials/one-cycle). 112 113 114 ## Good Usability 115 Only a few lines of code changes are needed to enable a PyTorch model to use DeepSpeed and ZeRO. Compared to current model parallelism libraries, DeepSpeed does not require a code redesign or model refactoring. It also does not put limitations on model dimensions (such as number of attention heads, hidden sizes, and others), batch size, or any other training parameters. For models of up to 13 billion parameters, you can use ZeRO-powered data parallelism conveniently without requiring model parallelism, while in contrast, standard data parallelism will run out of memory for models with more than 1.4 billion parameters. In addition, DeepSpeed conveniently supports flexible combination of ZeRO-powered data parallelism with custom model parallelisms, such as tensor slicing of NVIDIA's Megatron-LM. 116 117 118 ## Training 176 Enable 16-bit (FP16) training by in the `deepspeed_config` JSON. 177 ```json 178 "fp16": { 179 "enabled": true, 180 "loss_scale": 0, 181 "loss_scale_window": 1000, 182 "hysteresis": 2, 183 "consecutive_hysteresis": false, 184 "min_loss_scale": 1 185 } 186 ``` 187 188 ### Single-GPU, Multi-GPU, and Multi-Node Training 189 Easily switch between single-GPU, single-node multi-GPU, or multi-node multi-GPU 190 execution by specifying resources with a hostfile. 191 ```bash 192 deepspeed --hostfile= \ 193 \ 194 --deepspeed --deepspeed_config ds_config.json 195 ``` 196 The script `` will execute on the resources specified in 197 [``](/getting-started/#resource-configuration-multi-node). 198 199 ## Pipeline Parallelism 200 DeepSpeed provides [pipeline parallelism](/tutorials/pipeline/) for memory- 201 and communication- efficient training. DeepSpeed supports a hybrid 202 combination of data, model, and pipeline parallelism and has scaled to over 203 [one trillion parameters using 3D parallelism]({{ site.press_release_v3 }}). 204 Pipeline parallelism can also improve communication efficiency and has 205 accelerated training by up to 7x on low-bandwidth clusters. 206 207 208 ## Model Parallelism 209 ### Support for Custom Model Parallelism 210 DeepSpeed supports all forms of model parallelism including tensor slicing 211 based approaches such as the 212 [Megatron-LM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM). It does so by only 213 requiring the model parallelism framework to provide a *model parallelism 214 unit* (`mpu`) that implements a few bookkeeping functionalities: 215 216 ```python 217 mpu.get_model_parallel_rank() 218 mpu.get_model_parallel_group() 219 mpu.get_model_parallel_world_size() 220 221 mpu.get_data_parallel_rank() 222 mpu.get_data_parallel_group() 223 mpu.get_data_parallel_world_size() 224 ``` 225 226 ### Integration with Megatron-LM 227 DeepSpeed is fully compatible with [Megatron](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM). 228 Please see the [Megatron-LM tutorial](/tutorials/megatron/) for details. 229 230 231 232 233 ## The Zero Redundancy Optimizer 234 The Zero Redundancy Optimizer ([ZeRO](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054)) is at 235 the heart of DeepSpeed and enables large model training at a scale that is 236 simply not possible with model parallelism alone. When enabled, ZeRO allows 237 training models with over 13 billion parameters without any model parallelism, 238 and up to 200 billion parameter models with model parallelism on current 239 generation hardware. 240 241 For more details see the [ZeRO paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054), [GPT 242 tutorial](/tutorials/megatron/) on integration with 243 DeepSpeed. 244 245 ### Optimizer State and Gradient Partitioning 246 Optimizer State and Gradient Partitioning in ZeRO reduces the memory consumption of the 247 model states (optimizer states, gradients and parameters) by 8x compared to standard 248 data parallelism by partitioning these states across data parallel process instead of 249 replicating them. 250 251 ### Activation Partitioning 252 Activation Partitioning is a memory optimization in ZeRO that can reduce the memory 253 consumed by activations during model parallel training (MP). In MP certain 254 activations maybe required by all MP processes, resulting in a replication of 255 activations across MP GPUs. Activation Partitioning stores these activations in a 256 partitioned state once they are used for computation in the forward propagation. These 257 activations are allgathered right before they are needed again during the backward propagation. 258 By storing activations in a partitioned state, ZeRO in DeepSpeed can reduce the activation 259 memory footprint proportional to the MP degree. 260 261 ### Constant Buffer Optimization (CBO) 262 CBO enables high network and memory throughput while restricting memory usage to a 263 constant size. For memory- and network-bound operations such as normalization or 264 allreduce collectives, the performance depends on the size of the operand. Simply fusing 265 all operands into a single large operand can enable great throughput at the expense of 266 unnecessary memory overhead. CBO in DeepSpeed fuses smaller operands into approximately a 267 pre-defined sized buffer large enough to achieve great performance without the 268 unnecessary memory overhead. 269 270 ### Contiguous Memory Optimization (CMO) 271 CMO reduces memory fragmentation during training, preventing out of memory errors 272 due to lack of contiguous memory. Memory fragmentation is a result of interleaving between 273 short lived and long lived memory objects. During the forward propagation activation 274 checkpoints are long lived but the activations that recomputed are short lived. Similarly, 275 during the backward computation, the activation gradients are short lived while the parameter 276 gradients are long lived. CMO transfers activation checkpoints and parameter gradients 277 to contiguous buffers preventing memory fragmentation. 278 279 ## ZeRO-Offload 280 281 ZeRO-Offload pushes the boundary of the maximum model size that can be trained efficiently using minimal GPU resources, by exploiting computational and memory resources on both GPUs and their host CPUs. It allows training up to 13-billion-parameter models on a single NVIDIA V100 GPU, 10x larger than the state-of-the-art, while retaining high training throughput of over 30 teraflops per GPU. 282 283 For more details see the [ZeRO-Offload release blog]( https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/?p=689370&secret=iSlooB), and [tutorial](/tutorials/zero-offload/) on integration with DeepSpeed. 284 285 ## Additional Memory and Bandwidth Optimizations 286 287 ### Smart Gradient Accumulation 288 Gradient accumulation allows running larger batch size with limited memory by breaking an 289 effective batch into several sequential micro-batches, and averaging the parameter 290 gradients across these micro-batches. Furthermore, instead of averaging the gradients of 291 each micro-batch across all GPUs, the gradients are averaged locally during each step of 292 the sequence, and a single `allreduce` is done at the end of the sequence to produce the 293 averaged gradients for the effective batch across all GPUs. This strategy significantly 294 reduces the communication involved over the approach of averaging globally for each 295 micro-batch, specially when the number of micro-batches per effective batch is large. 296 297 ### Communication Overlapping 298 During back propagation, DeepSpeed can overlap the communication required for averaging 299 parameter gradients that have already been computed with the ongoing gradient computation. 300 This computation-communication overlap allows DeepSpeed to achieve higher throughput even 301 at modest batch sizes. 302 303 ## Training Features 304 305 ### Simplified training API 306 The DeepSpeed core API consists of just a handful of methods: 307 * initialization: `initialize` 308 * training: `backward` and `step` 309 * argument parsing: `add_config_arguments` 310 * checkpointing : `load_checkpoint` and `store_checkpoint` 311 312 DeepSpeed supports most of the features described in this document, via the use of these API, 313 along with a `deepspeed_config` JSON file for enabling and disabling the features. 314 Please see the [core API doc](https://deepspeed.readthedocs.io/) for more details. 315 316 ### Activation Checkpointing API 317 318 DeepSpeed's Activation Checkpointing API supports activation checkpoint partitioning, 319 cpu checkpointing, and contiguous memory optimizations, while also allowing layerwise 320 profiling. Please see the [core API doc](https://deepspeed.readthedocs.io/) for more details. 321 322 323 ### Gradient Clipping 324 ```json 325 { 326 "gradient_clipping": 1.0 327 } 328 ``` 329 DeepSpeed handles gradient clipping under the hood based on the max gradient norm 330 specified by the user. 331 Please see the [core API doc](https://deepspeed.readthedocs.io/) for more details. 332 333 ### Automatic loss scaling with mixed precision 334 DeepSpeed internally handles loss scaling for mixed precision training. The parameters 335 for loss scaling can be specified in the `deepspeed_config` JSON file. 336 Please see the [core API doc](https://deepspeed.readthedocs.io/) for more details. 337 338 ## Training Optimizers 339 340 ### Fused Adam optimizer and arbitrary torch.optim.Optimizer 341 With DeepSpeed, the user can choose to use a high performance implementation of ADAM from 342 NVIDIA, or any training optimizer that extends torch's `torch.optim.Optimizer` class. 343 344 ### CPU-Adam: High-Performance vectorized implementation of Adam 345 We introduce an efficient implementation of Adam optimizer on CPU that improves the parameter-update 346 performance by nearly an order of magnitude. We use the AVX SIMD instructions on Intel-x86 architecture 347 for the CPU-Adam implementation. We support both AVX-512 and AVX-2 instruction sets. DeepSpeed uses 348 AVX-2 by default which can be switched to AVX-512 by setting the build flag, `DS_BUILD_AVX512` to 1 when 349 installing DeepSpeed. Using AVX-512, we observe 5.1x to 6.5x speedups considering the model-size between 350 1 to 10 billion parameters with respect to torch-adam. 351 352 ### Memory bandwidth optimized FP16 Optimizer 353 Mixed precision training is handled by the DeepSpeed FP16 Optimizer. This optimizer not 354 only handles FP16 training but is also highly efficient. The performance of weight update 355 is primarily dominated by the memory bandwidth, and the achieved memory bandwidth is 356 dependent on the size of the input operands. The FP16 Optimizer is designed to maximize 357 the achievable memory bandwidth by merging all the parameters of the model into a single 358 large buffer, and applying the weight updates in a single kernel, allowing it to achieve 359 high memory bandwidth. 360 361 ### Large Batch Training with LAMB Optimizer 362 363 DeepSpeed makes it easy to train with large batch sizes by enabling the LAMB Optimizer. 364 For more details on LAMB, see the [LAMB paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.00962.pdf). 365 366 ### Memory-Efficient Training with ZeRO Optimizer 367 DeepSpeed can train models with up to 13 billion parameters without model parallelism, and 368 models with up to 200 billion parameters with 16-way model parallelism. This leap in 369 model size is possible through the memory efficiency achieved via the ZeRO Optimizer. For 370 more details see [ZeRO paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054) . 371 372 373 374 ## Training Agnostic Checkpointing 375 DeepSpeed can simplify checkpointing for you regardless of whether you are using data 376 parallel training, model parallel training, mixed-precision training, a mix of these 377 three, or using the zero optimizer to enable larger model sizes. 378 Please see the [Getting Started](/getting-started/) guide 379 and the [core API doc](https://deepspeed.readthedocs.io/) for more details. 380 381 ## Advanced parameter search 382 DeepSpeed supports multiple Learning Rate Schedules to enable faster convergence for 383 large batch scaling. 384 385 ### Learning Rate Range Test 386 Please refer to the [Learning Rate Range Test](/tutorials/lrrt/) tutorial. 387 388 ### 1Cycle Learning Rate Schedule 389 Please refer to the [1Cycle Learning Rate Schedule](/tutorials/one-cycle/) tutorial. 390 391 392 ## Simplified Data Loader 393 DeepSpeed abstracts away data parallelism and model parallelism from the user when it 394 comes to data loading. Users simply provide a PyTorch dataset, and DeepSpeed data loader 395 can automatically handle batch creation appropriately. 396 397 ## Data Efficiency 398 Please refer to the [Data Efficiency](/tutorials/data-efficiency/) tutorial. 399 400 ## Performance Analysis and Debugging 401 402 DeepSpeed provides a set of tools for performance analysis and debugging. 403 404 ### Wall Clock Breakdown 405 406 DeepSpeed provides a detailed breakdown of the time spent 407 in different parts of the training. 408 This can be enabled by setting the following in the `deepspeed_config` file. 409 410 ```json 411 { 412 "wall_clock_breakdown": true, 413 } 414 415 ``` 416 417 ### Timing Activation Checkpoint Functions 418 419 When activation checkpointing is enabled, profiling the forward and backward time of each checkpoint function can be enabled in the `deepspeed_config` file. 420 421 ```json 422 { 423 "activation_checkpointing": { 424 "profile": true 425 } 426 } 427 428 ``` 429 430 ### Flops Profiler 431 432 The DeepSpeed flops profiler measures the time, flops and parameters of a PyTorch model and shows which modules or layers are the bottleneck. When used with the DeepSpeed runtime, the flops profiler can be configured in the `deepspeed_config` file as follows: 433 434 ```json 435 { 436 "flops_profiler": { 437 "enabled": true, 438 "profile_step": 1, 439 "module_depth": -1, 440 "top_modules": 3, 441 "detailed": true, 442 } 443 } 444 445 ``` 446 The flops profiler can also be used as a standalone package. Please refer to the [Flops Profiler](/tutorials/flops-profiler) tutorial for more details. 447 448 449 ### Autotuning 450 451 The DeepSpeed Autotuner uses model information, system information, and heuristics to efficiently tune Zero stage, micro batch size, and other Zero configurations. Using the autotuning feature requires no code change from DeepSpeed users. While `"autotuning": {"enabled": true}` is the minimal required to enable autotuning, there are other parameters users can define to configure the autotuning process. Below shows major parameters and their default values in the autotuning configuration. Please refer to the [Autotuning](/tutorials/autotuning) tutorial for more details. 452 453 ```json 454 { 455 "autotuning": { 456 "enabled": true, 457 "results_dir": null, 458 "exps_dir": null, 459 "overwrite": false, 460 "metric": "throughput", 461 "num_nodes": null, 462 "num_gpus": null, 463 "start_profile_step": 3, 464 "end_profile_step": 5, 465 "fast": true, 466 "num_tuning_micro_batch_sizes": 3, 467 "tuner_type": "model_based", 468 "tuner_early_stopping": 5, 469 "tuner_num_trials": 50, 470 "arg_mappings": null 471 } 472 } 473 474 ``` 475 The flops profiler can also be used as a standalone package. Please refer to the [Flops Profiler](/tutorials/flops-profiler) tutorial for more details. 476 477 ### Monitor 478 479 The DeepSpeed Monitor logs live training metrics to one or more monitoring backends, including PyTorch's [TensorBoard](https://pytorch.org/docs/1.8.0/tensorboard.html), [WandB](https://docs.wandb.ai/quickstart), or simply to CSV files. The Monitor can be configured with one or more backends in the `deepspeed_config` file as follows: 480 481 ```json 482 { 483 "tensorboard": { 484 "enabled": true, 485 "output_path": "output/ds_logs/", 486 "job_name": "train_bert" 487 } 488 "wandb": { 489 "enabled": true, 490 "team": "my_team", 491 "group": "my_group", 492 "project": "my_project" 493 } 494 "csv_monitor": { 495 "enabled": true, 496 "output_path": "output/ds_logs/", 497 "job_name": "train_bert" 498 } 499 } 500 501 ``` 502 503 The Monitor can also be added to log custom metrics and client codes. Please refer to the [Monitor](/tutorials/monitor) tutorial for more details. 504 505 ### Communication Logging 506 507 DeepSpeed provides logging of all communication operations launched within `deepspeed.comm`. The communication logger can be configured in the `deepspeed_config` file as follows: 508 509 ```json 510 { 511 "comms_logger": { 512 "enabled": true, 513 "verbose": false, 514 "prof_all": true, 515 "debug": false 516 } 517 } 518 519 ``` 520 521 Client codes can then print a summary with a call to `deepspeed.comm.log_summary()`. For more details and example usage, see the [Communication Logging](/tutorials/comms-logging) tutorial. 522 523 ## Mixture of Experts (MoE) 524 To learn more about training Mixture of Experts (MoE) models with DeepSpeed, see our [tutorial](https://www.deepspeed.ai/tutorials/mixture-of-experts/) for more details. 525

You can read more about this in the original blog post [here](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/tree/master/blogs/windows/08-2024/README.md). Among features that are currently not supported are async io (AIO) and GDS (which does not support Windows). 1. Install PyTorch, such as pytorch 2.3+cu121. 2. Install Visual C++ build tools, such as VS2022 C++ x64/x86 build tools. 3. Launch Cmd console with Administrator permissions for creating required symlink folders and ensure MSVC tools are added to your PATH or launch the Developer Command Prompt for Visual Studio 2022 with administrator permissions. 4. Run `build_win.bat` to build wheel in `dist` folder. # Further Reading All DeepSpeed documentation, tutorials, and blogs can be found on our website: [deepspeed.ai](https://www.deepspeed.ai/) | | Description | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | [Getting Started](https://www.deepspeed.ai/getting-started/) | First steps with DeepSpeed | | [DeepSpeed JSON Configuration](https://www.deepspeed.ai/docs/config-json/) | Configuring DeepSpeed | | [API Documentation](https://deepspeed.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) | Generated DeepSpeed API documentation | | [Tutorials](https://www.deepspeed.ai/tutorials/) | Tutorials | | [Blogs](https://www.deepspeed.ai/posts/) | Blogs | # CI funding This being an open source project we rely on others to provide us resources for CI hardware. At this moment Modal is kindly supporting our GPU CI runs by funding the hardware for us. Modal is an AI infrastructure platform for inference, fine-tuning, batch jobs and more. Get started with $30/mo in free credits today at https://modal.com. We have been getting an amazing support from Modal's team and will surely recommend them to your business. # Contributing DeepSpeed welcomes your contributions! Please see our [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) guide for more details on formatting, testing, etc.
Thanks so much to all of our amazing contributors! ## Developer Certificate of Origin This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions require you to agree to a Developer Certificate of Origin [DCO](https://wiki.linuxfoundation.org/dco) stating that they agree to the terms published at https://developercertificate.org for that *particular* contribution. DCOs are per-commit, so each commit needs to be signed off. These can be signed in the commit by adding the `-s` flag. DCO enforcement can also be signed off in the PR itself by clicking on the DCO enforcement check. ## Code of Conduct This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/). For more information see the [Code of Conduct FAQ](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/faq/) or contact [opencode@microsoft.com](mailto:opencode@microsoft.com) with any additional questions or comments. # Publications 1. input.content:
# DeepSpeed 项目全景：大模型训练为什么需要它

> 本讲是整本学习手册的第一讲。你不写一行 DeepSpeed 代码，只需要建立三样东西：对项目定位的认知、对文档地图的熟悉、对版本机制的把握。它们是后续所有源码阅读的坐标系。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清楚 DeepSpeed 解决的三大核心痛点：**显存墙**（模型放不进显存）、**通信墙**（多卡之间数据搬运太慢）、**训练吞吐**（整体训练太慢）。
2. 列举 DeepSpeed 的代表性系统创新：**ZeRO**、**ZeRO-Infinity / ZeRO-Offload**、**3D-Parallelism**、**Ulysses 序列并行**、**DeepSpeed-MoE** 等。
3. 知道仓库当前版本（0.19.9）、文档入口（deepspeed.ai 与 `docs/` 目录），以及它与 HuggingFace Transformers / Accelerate / Lightning 等框架的集成关系。
4. 学会用 `git log` 观察一个开源项目「最近在忙什么」，把 README 的新闻列表和实际代码提交互相印证。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲几乎不需要分布式训练背景，但以下概念会反复出现，先用大白话解释：

- **参数量 Ψ（psi）**：模型里所有可训练权重标量的总数。一个 7B 模型有约 70 亿个参数。显存讨论中常用 Ψ 代指「参数个数」。
- **数据并行（Data Parallelism, DP）**：每张卡都持有**完整的**模型副本，各自吃不同批次的数据，反向传播后同步梯度。最易用，但每张卡都重复存一份模型状态——这就是显存浪费的根源。
- **显存墙（memory wall）**：以混合精度 + Adam 优化器为例，除了参数本身，还要存梯度和优化器状态（Adam 的一阶/二阶动量、fp32 主权重）。粗略估算，训练状态约占

  \[ 2\Psi(\text{fp16 参数}) + 2\Psi(\text{fp16 梯度}) + 12\Psi(\text{fp32 优化器状态}) = 16\Psi \text{ 字节} \]

  一个 7B 模型仅模型状态就需要约 112 GB，而单卡显存通常只有 40~96 GB——模型还没跑起来就「撞墙」了。
- **通信墙（communication wall）**：多卡训练要在卡间搬运梯度/参数。当通信时间接近甚至超过计算时间，加卡不再提速。
- **ZeRO（Zero Redundancy Optimizer）**：DeepSpeed 的招牌技术。核心想法一句话：数据并行下每张卡都存了**完整副本**，这是冗余的；ZeRO 把优化器状态、梯度、参数逐级**切分**到各卡上，用时再临时聚合，从而用「通信换显存」。细节在单元 5 展开，本讲只需记住它是 DeepSpeed 的立身之本。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲涉及的文件很少，都是「项目门面」级别的文件：

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | 项目第一入口：新闻、定位、集成生态、硬件支持表、安装方式、论文列表 |
| `docs/_pages/training.md` | 官网「训练总览」页面的源文件，相当于官方版能力矩阵与特性清单 |
| `version.txt` | 单行文件，记录当前版本号（0.19.9），是发布线的源头 |
| `setup.py` | 安装脚本，从这里消费 `version.txt` |
| `deepspeed/__init__.py` | 主包入口，把版本号暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__` |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 README 的能力矩阵

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

读一个大型开源项目的第一步不是看代码，而是读它的 README，并从中提炼出一张「能力矩阵」：**它解决什么问题、靠什么技术解决、和谁协作、支持什么硬件**。

DeepSpeed 的 README 把这些信息分散在几个板块里：

| README 板块 | 回答的问题 |
| --- | --- |
| Latest News（L27 起） | 项目最近在往哪个方向演进 |
| Extreme Speed and Scale（L71 起） | 项目一句话定位与核心创新点 |
| DeepSpeed Adoption（L79 起） | 哪些著名大模型用它训出来、与哪些框架集成 |
| Build Pipeline Status（L110 起） | 在哪些硬件平台上跑 CI（即官方背书的平台） |
| Installation / HW support（L123 起） | 怎么装、支持哪些加速器 |
| Publications（L223 起） | 每项技术对应的论文 |

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把 README 当地图来「测绘」的流程：

1. 先看定位句（Extreme Speed and Scale 段），抓住核心创新关键词。
2. 再看 Latest News，按时间倒序扫一遍，找出反复出现的主题（这些就是活跃战线）。
3. 然后看 Adoption 与集成表，确认生态位：它是「库」，被上层框架调用，而不是取代它们。

### 4.2 训练文档结构

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`docs/` 目录是 DeepSpeed 官网（deepspeed.ai）的源文件，用 Jekyll 构建。其中 `docs/_pages/training.md` 是官网「Training Overview and Features」页面的源文件——可以把它理解为**官方版能力矩阵**：README 用一段话告诉你「有什么」，training.md 用整篇文档告诉你「每项特性具体是什么、怎么开」。

这个文件有个有趣的细节：它实际上包含**两个 Jekyll 页面**（两段 front matter），前半部分是 `/training/`（训练总览），后半部分是 `/features/`（特性详解）。读它时要意识到自己在「两页文档」之间穿越。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

training.md 的叙事结构本身就是一条问题-方案链，推荐按这个顺序读：

```
训练大模型难（Overview, L9-17）
  ├─ 要自己搭分布式/混合精度/梯度累积/检查点 → DeepSpeed API 轻量包装 PyTorch（L19-27）
  ├─ 太慢 → Speed：BERT-large 44 分钟、GPT-2 3.75x（L29-52）
  ├─ 显存不够 → Memory efficiency：ZeRO、ZeRO-Offload（L56-77）
  ├─ 规模上天 → Scalability：3D 并行、万亿参数（L79-96）
  ├─ 网络带宽差 → Communication efficiency：流水线并行降通信（L98-100）
  ├─ 数据太多 → Data efficiency：课程学习、token dropping（L102-103）
  ├─ 收敛太慢 → LAMB 等大 batch 优化器（L105-111）
  └─ 都想要但怕难用 → Good usability：几行代码接入（L114-115）
```

前半部分以「叙事」收尾于一张特性清单（L118-163）；后半部分（L165 起）逐项展开每个特性的细节与配置片段。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① 问题描述：为什么需要 DeepSpeed。** 文档开篇直接点出双重痛点——既要搭好分布式/混合精度这些「样板代码」，又可能得不到理想的性能；大模型在纯数据并行下显存直接爆掉，而模型并行又难用：

见 [training.md:L9-L17](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L9-L17)。这句「a large model easily runs out of memory with pure data parallelism」就是第 2 节讲的显存墙的官方表述。

**② 产品哲学：轻量包装，不另起炉灶。** DeepSpeed API 被定位为「PyTorch 之上的轻量包装」——你仍用 PyTorch 的一切，DeepSpeed 接管分布式训练、混合精度、梯度累积、检查点这些样板技术，见 [training.md:L19-L27](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L19-L27)。这解释了为什么手册单元 2 讲 `initialize()` 时你会看到：模型、优化器、数据加载器都还是 PyTorch 对象，DeepSpeed 只是「包」了一层引擎。

**③ 显存效率：ZeRO 的官方定义。** 文档给出了 ZeRO 的一句话定义——与普通数据并行「复制」模型状态不同，ZeRO 把模型状态和梯度「切分」到各数据并行进程上，见 [training.md:L62-L69](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L62-L69)。同一节还给出量化对比：单卡 13B 参数 vs 传统 DDP 约 1.4B 就 OOM（L57-L60），ZeRO-2 最多省 8 倍内存（L66-L67）；ZeRO-Offload 进一步用「单张 V100 训 13B」打开局面，见 [training.md:L77](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L77)。

**④ 可扩展性与 3D 并行。** 「3D 并行」= 数据并行 + 张量并行 + 流水线并行三者组合，官方文档说明它支撑过万亿参数模型，见 [training.md:L79-L88](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L79-L88)。这三个维度分别对应单元 5（ZeRO 数据并行）、单元 6（张量/序列并行、流水线并行）。

**⑤ 核心 API 清单。** 文档后半部分总结了 DeepSpeed 的核心 API，只有寥寥几个方法：`initialize`、`backward`、`step`、`add_config_arguments`、`load_checkpoint` / `store_checkpoint`，见 [training.md:L305-L314](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L305-L314)。这是单元 2 的预习提纲：整个训练引擎对用户暴露的入口就这么几个。

**⑥ 特性深读区（后半页）。** 从 [training.md:L233-L259](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L233-L259) 开始逐项解释 ZeRO 的子优化（优化器状态与梯度切分、激活切分、恒定缓冲区优化 CBO、连续内存优化 CMO）——这四个名词在单元 5 读 `stage_1_and_2.py` / `stage3.py` 时会一一对应到具体代码。ZeRO-Offload 的展开说明见 [training.md:L279-L283](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L279-L283)。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：training.md 中 ZeRO 的官方一句话定义是什么？它和数据并行的本质区别在哪里？

答案：ZeRO 与「在数据并行进程间复制内存状态」的基本数据并行不同，它把模型状态（model states）和梯度**切分（partition）**到各进程以节省内存（见 [training.md:L62-L65](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L62-L65)）。本质区别：复制 vs 切分——切分换来的是显存节省，付出的是用时需临时通信聚合。

**练习 2**：文档说 DeepSpeed 的核心 API「只有一把手能数得过来的几个方法」，请列举它们。

答案：`initialize`（初始化）、`backward` 和 `step`（训练）、`add_config_arguments`（参数解析）、`load_checkpoint` 和 `store_checkpoint`（检查点），见 [training.md:L305-L310](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L305-L310)。

**练习 3**：「3D 并行」中的三个维度是什么？ZeRO 在其中扮演哪个维度？

答案：数据并行、张量/模型并行、流水线并行（见 [training.md:L80-L82](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L80-L82)）。ZeRO 强化的是数据并行这一维（内存高效的数据并行），且可与另外两类并行组合。

### 4.3 版本与发布线

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

「这个仓库现在是哪个版本？」看似简单，但在 DeepSpeed 里版本信息有一条清晰的**传递链**：

```
version.txt（唯一事实来源，当前 0.19.9）
   ├─→ setup.py 打包时读取 → PyPI 发布的包版本
   └─→ (构建期写入) deepspeed/git_version_info.py
          └─→ deepspeed/__init__.py 导出 __version__ / __git_hash__ / __git_branch__
```

理解这条链的意义在于：**用户看到的 `deepspeed.__version__` 与仓库里的 `version.txt` 是同源的**；而且 DeepSpeed 还把 git 提交哈希打进包里，运行时日志会打印 version + git-hash + git-branch，这对你排查「线上到底跑的是哪份代码」极其有用（阅读源码时也能用它确认代码与讲义引用的 HEAD 一致）。

另一个要点是**发布节奏**：DeepSpeed 是「rolling master」模式——master 分支持续合入，定期打 tag 发 PyPI。所以 `git log` 里的最新提交就是最真实的项目动态，比新闻列表更细粒度。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

版本信息的生命周期：

1. 开发期：`version.txt` 由维护者更新，`0.19.9` 表示主版本 0、次版本 19、补丁版本 9。
2. 构建期：`setup.py` 读取 `version.txt`；如果设置了 `DS_BUILD_STRING` 环境变量则附加 `.devX` 后缀，否则把 git 哈希写入版本串，并生成 `deepspeed/git_version_info.py`。
3. 运行期：`import deepspeed` 时从 `git_version_info` 导入 version / git_hash / git_branch，暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__`、`deepspeed.__git_hash__`。
4. 日志期：每次 `initialize()` 都会打印 `DeepSpeed info: version=..., git-hash=..., git-branch=...`。

**① 唯一事实来源：version.txt。** 整个文件只有一行：

见 [setup.py:L228-L229](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/setup.py#L228-L229)，注释明确写着「Parse the DeepSpeed version string from version.txt」。紧随其后（L231 起）的逻辑决定是否附加 `.dev` 后缀或 git 哈希。

见 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L70](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L70)，从 `git_version_info`（构建时生成）导入 version、git_hash、git_branch；随后在 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L75-L85](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L75-L85) 解析出主/次/补丁三元组并导出 `__version__`、`__git_hash__`、`__git_branch__`。同一个文件里，[deepspeed/__init__.py:L88](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L88) 附近的 `dist = None` 是个伏笔：分布式通信句柄被设计为延迟绑定（引擎初始化时才指向 `deepspeed.comm`），单元 3 会展开。

#### 4.3.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：验证版本传递链的三环都指向同一个版本号。

**操作步骤**：

1. `cat version.txt` → 记下输出（预期 `0.19.9`）。
2. `grep -n "version.txt" setup.py` → 确认 setup.py 第 229 行在读取它。
3. 若本地已安装 deepspeed：`python -c "import deepspeed; print(deepspeed.__version__, deepspeed.__git_hash__)"` → 对比输出与第 1 步结果，并核对 `__git_hash__` 的前 9 位是否等于 `git rev-parse --short=9 HEAD`（本仓库 HEAD 为 `dc046b15d`）。
4. `pip index versions deepspeed 2>/dev/null || pip install deepspeed==` → 观察 PyPI 上可用的版本列表，看看 0.19.9 处在发布线的什么位置。

**需要观察的现象**：第 3 步中 `__version__` 与 `version.txt` 一致；若你是 `pip install deepspeed` 装的正式发行版，`__git_hash__` 是打包那次提交的哈希；若是源码 editable 安装（`pip install -e .`），哈希应与你本地 HEAD 一致。

**预期结果**：三个环节读出的版本号完全一致。第 3、4 步依赖本地 Python 环境，**待本地验证**。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：DeepSpeed 的版本号「唯一事实来源」是哪个文件？当前值是多少？

答案：仓库根目录的 `version.txt`，当前值为 `0.19.9`（见 [version.txt:L1](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/version.txt#L1)）。

**练习 2**：为什么 `deepspeed.__version__` 之外还要导出 `__git_hash__`？举一个实际用途。

答案：因为 PyPI 版本号更新有间隔，而 rolling master 每天都有合入，仅凭 `0.19.9` 无法区分「同一版本号下不同的代码状态」。`__git_hash__`（见 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L84](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L84)）能精确定位到具体提交。实际用途：报 bug 时把 `initialize()` 日志里的 version/git-hash 行贴出来，维护者即可复现你的代码版本；本手册也用它保证所有永久链接指向同一提交。

**练习 3**：如果不小心删除了 `version.txt`，安装（`pip install -e .`）会在哪一步失败？

答案：在 `setup.py` 执行到 [setup.py:L229](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/setup.py#L229) 的 `open('version.txt', 'r')` 时直接抛 `FileNotFoundError`，打包元数据无法生成。这体现了该文件作为唯一事实来源的地位。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：写一份 1 页的《DeepSpeed 活跃方向调研笔记》——用 git 历史与 README 新闻互相印证。**

一份开源项目的「自我介绍」（README News）和它的「实际行为」（git log）对照着读，是判断项目健康度和方向的最快方法。本实践把前面三个模块串起来。

**实践目标**：从真实提交记录中识别出 3 个正在积极演进的子系统，并与 README 的 Latest News 互相印证。

**操作步骤**：

1. 进入仓库根目录，执行：

   ```bash
   git log --oneline -20
   ```

2. 把输出按主题分组。分组线索：提交信息开头的方括号标签（`[Hybrid Engine]`、`[AutoEP]`、`[AffineIR]`、`[VocabTP]`）和前缀（`ZeRO-1/2:`、`ZeRO-3:`、`ci:`）。
3. 打开 [README.md:L27-L67](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L27-L67) 的 Latest News（含 More news），为每个分组找一条时间上最近的新闻佐证。
4. 用 `git log --oneline -20 -- deepspeed/runtime/zero/` 这样的路径过滤命令，分别统计各主题目录的提交热度。
5. 写成 1 页笔记，每个方向包含：方向名、证据提交（哈希 + 一句话）、README 佐证新闻（日期 + 标题）、一句话判断它解决的是显存墙 / 通信墙 / 吞吐中的哪一个。

**参考范例**（以下为撰写本讲时对 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的真实观察，可作为你的笔记样例）：

- **ZeRO 卸载与显存优化**：`dc046b15d`「ZeRO-1/2: preserve gradients across request boundaries until step」、`c6291b7e1`「ZeRO-3: copy offloaded master weights back to the device through pinned buffer」——佐证新闻：SuperOffload 获 ASPLOS 2026 提名（2026/03）、ZenFlow（2025/08）。主攻**显存墙**。
- **专家并行 AutoEP / AffineIR**：`66fef47b2`、`f81850499`、`12ffb9903`、`7501610ee` 四条 AutoEP/AffineIR 相关提交——佐证新闻：Ray x DeepSpeed Meetup 中提到的专家并行与 fused kernel 工作（2025/10）。主攻**吞吐与显存**。
- **混合引擎与张量并行**：`ab7fd98fa`「[Hybrid Engine] Enable graph capture ... on non-CUDA accelerators」、`1a956270f`「[VocabTP] vocab_parallel_ce support fused LM-head projection + loss」——佐证新闻：AutoTP（2025/03，More news）。主攻**推理/训练一体化与通信墙**。

**需要观察的现象**：git log 的主题分布与 README 新闻的优先级高度吻合——新闻是「宣言」，提交是「行动」；两者不一致的地方（例如某特性上了新闻但近期无提交）通常意味着该方向已进入稳定维护期。

**预期结果**：一份含 3 个方向、每个方向有提交证据 + 新闻佐证 + 一句话定位的 1 页笔记。完成后建议存档在 `DeepSpeed-tutorial/` 之外的自有笔记目录里，学习单元 5 和单元 6 时回头验证你的判断。

## 6. 本讲小结

- DeepSpeed 是面向超大模型训练与推理的**底层优化库**，三大痛点是**显存墙、通信墙、训练吞吐**；核心创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D 并行、Ulysses 序列并行与 DeepSpeed-MoE（[README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)）。

- 阅读 »README News + git log« 双轨对照是判断开源项目活跃方向的标准手法；当前最活跃的三条线是 ZeRO 卸载（ZenFlow/SuperOffload 系）、专家并行（AutoEP/AffineIR）、混合引擎/张量并行。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

2. 通读一遍 [README.md:L123-L169](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L123-L169) 的安装章节，留意「JIT 编译」与「预编译」两种算子构建方式的区别——这是 u1-l3 的主题。

# DeepSpeed 项目全景：大模型训练为什么需要它

> 本讲是整本学习手册的第一讲。你不写一行 DeepSpeed 代码，只需要建立三样东西：对项目定位的认知、对文档地图的熟悉、对版本机制的把握。它们是后续所有源码阅读的坐标系。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清楚 DeepSpeed 解决的三大核心痛点：**显存墙**（模型放不进显存）、**通信墙**（多卡之间数据搬运太慢）、**训练吞吐**（整体训练太慢）。
2. 列举 DeepSpeed 的代表性系统创新：**ZeRO**、**ZeRO-Infinity / ZeRO-Offload**、**3D-Parallelism**、**Ulysses 序列并行**、**DeepSpeed-MoE** 等。
3. 知道仓库当前版本（0.19.9）、文档入口（deepspeed.ai 与 `docs/` 目录），以及它与 HuggingFace Transformers / Accelerate / Lightning 等框架的集成关系。
4. 学会用 `git log` 观察一个开源项目「最近在忙什么」，把 README 的新闻列表和实际代码提交互相印证。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲几乎不需要分布式训练背景，但以下概念会反复出现，先用大白话解释：

- **参数量 Ψ（psi）**：模型里所有可训练权重标量的总数。一个 7B 模型有约 70 亿个参数。显存讨论中常用 Ψ 代指「参数个数」。
- **数据并行（Data Parallelism, DP）**：每张卡都持有**完整的**模型副本，各自吃不同批次的数据，反向传播后同步梯度。最易用，但每张卡都重复存一份模型状态——这就是显存浪费的根源。
- **显存墙（memory wall）**：以混合精度 + Adam 优化器为例，除了参数本身，还要存梯度和优化器状态（Adam 的一阶/二阶动量、fp32 主权重）。粗略估算，训练状态约占

  \[ 2\Psi(\text{fp16 参数}) + 2\Psi(\text{fp16 梯度}) + 12\Psi(\text{fp32 优化器状态}) = 16\Psi \text{ 字节} \]

  一个 7B 模型仅模型状态就需要约 112 GB，而单卡显存通常只有 40~96 GB——模型还没跑起来就「撞墙」了。
- **通信墙（communication wall）**：多卡训练要在卡间搬运梯度/参数。当通信时间接近甚至超过计算时间，加卡不再提速。
- **ZeRO（Zero Redundancy Optimizer）**：DeepSpeed 的招牌技术。核心想法一句话：数据并行下每张卡都存了**完整副本**，这是冗余的；ZeRO 把优化器状态、梯度、参数逐级**切分**到各卡上，用时再临时聚合，从而用「通信换显存」。细节在单元 5 展开，本讲只需记住它是 DeepSpeed 的立身之本。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲涉及的文件很少，都是「项目门面」级别的文件：

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | 项目第一入口：新闻、定位、集成生态、硬件支持表、安装方式、论文列表 |
| `docs/_pages/training.md` | 官网「训练总览」页面的源文件，相当于官方版能力矩阵与特性清单 |
| `version.txt` | 单行文件，记录当前版本号（0.19.9），是发布线的源头 |
| `setup.py` | 安装脚本，从这里消费 `version.txt` |
| `deepspeed/__init__.py` | 主包入口，把版本号暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__` |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 README 的能力矩阵

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

读一个大型开源项目的第一步不是看代码，而是读它的 README，并从中提炼出一张「能力矩阵」：**它解决什么问题、靠什么技术解决、和谁协作、支持什么硬件**。

DeepSpeed 的 README 把这些信息分散在几个板块里：

| README 板块 | 回答的问题 |
| --- | --- |
| Latest News（L27 起） | 项目最近在往哪个方向演进 |
| Extreme Speed and Scale（L71 起） | 项目一句话定位与核心创新点 |
| DeepSpeed Adoption（L79 起） | 哪些著名大模型用它训出来、与哪些框架集成 |
| Build Pipeline Status（L110 起） | 在哪些硬件平台上跑 CI（即官方背书的平台） |
| Installation / HW support（L123 起） | 怎么装、支持哪些加速器 |
| Publications（L223 起） | 每项技术对应的论文 |

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把 README 当地图来「测绘」的流程：

1. 先看定位句（Extreme Speed and Scale 段），抓住核心创新关键词。
2. 再看 Latest News，按时间倒序扫一遍，找出反复出现的主题（这些就是活跃战线）。
3. 然后看 Adoption 与集成表，确认生态位：它是「库」，被上层框架调用，而不是取代它们。
4. 最后看 Build Pipeline / HW support 表，确认硬件矩阵，这决定了后续读源码时会遇到的多后端抽象（单元 3 会讲）。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① 一句话定位与五大创新点。** README 在标题段直接列出了 DeepSpeed 的系统创新清单：

> 这些创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D-Parallelism、Ulysses Sequence Parallelism、DeepSpeed-MoE 等。

见 [README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)。这段话就是整本学习手册的「课程大纲」：单元 5 讲 ZeRO 系列，单元 6 讲 3D 并行 / Ulysses / MoE。README 还点出 DeepSpeed 训练过 MT-530B、BLOOM 等当时的最大模型，见 [README.md:L84-L95](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L84-L95)。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：亲手从 README 提炼出一张属于自己的能力矩阵表。

**操作步骤**：

1. 打开仓库根目录的 `README.md`（本讲用 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的版本）。

### 4.2 训练文档结构

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`docs/` 目录是 DeepSpeed 官网（deepspeed.ai）的源文件，用 Jekyll 构建。其中 `docs/_pages/training.md` 是官网「Training Overview and Features」页面的源文件——可以把它理解为**官方版能力矩阵**：README 用一段话告诉你「有什么」，training.md 用整篇文档告诉你「每项特性具体是什么、怎么开」。

这个文件有个有趣的细节：它实际上包含**两个 Jekyll 页面**（两段 front matter），前半部分是 `/training/`（训练总览），后半部分是 `/features/`（特性详解）。读它时要意识到自己在「两页文档」之间穿越。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

training.md 的叙事结构本身就是一条问题-方案链，推荐按这个顺序读：

```
训练大模型难（Overview, L9-17）
  ├─ 要自己搭分布式/混合精度/梯度累积/检查点 → DeepSpeed API 轻量包装 PyTorch（L19-27）
  ├─ 太慢 → Speed：BERT-large 44 分钟、GPT-2 3.75x（L29-52）
  ├─ 显存不够 → Memory efficiency：ZeRO、ZeRO-Offload（L56-77）
  ├─ 规模上天 → Scalability：3D 并行、万亿参数（L79-96）
  ├─ 网络带宽差 → Communication efficiency：流水线并行降通信（L98-100）
  ├─ 数据太多 → Data efficiency：课程学习、token dropping（L102-103）
  ├─ 收敛太慢 → LAMB 等大 batch 优化器（L105-111）
  └─ 都想要但怕难用 → Good usability：几行代码接入（L114-115）
```

前半部分以「叙事」收尾于一张特性清单（L118-163）；后半部分（L165 起）逐项展开每个特性的细节与配置片段。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① 问题描述：为什么需要 DeepSpeed。** 文档开篇直接点出双重痛点——既要搭好分布式/混合精度这些「样板代码」，又可能得不到理想的性能；大模型在纯数据并行下显存直接爆掉，而模型并行又难用：

见 [training.md:L9-L17](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L9-L17)。这句「a large model easily runs out of memory with pure data parallelism」就是第 2 节讲的显存墙的官方表述。

**② 产品哲学：轻量包装，不另起炉灶。** DeepSpeed API 被定位为「PyTorch 之上的轻量包装」——你仍用 PyTorch 的一切，DeepSpeed 接管分布式训练、混合精度、梯度累积、检查点这些样板技术，见 [training.md:L19-L27](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L19-L27)。这解释了为什么手册单元 2 讲 `initialize()` 时你会看到：模型、优化器、数据加载器都还是 PyTorch 对象，DeepSpeed 只是「包」了一层引擎。

**③ 显存效率：ZeRO 的官方定义。** 文档给出了 ZeRO 的一句话定义——与普通数据并行「复制」模型状态不同，ZeRO 把模型状态和梯度「切分」到各数据并行进程上，见 [training.md:L62-L69](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L62-L69)。同一节还给出量化对比：单卡 13B 参数 vs 传统 DDP 约 1.4B 就 OOM（L57-L60），ZeRO-2 最多省 8 倍内存（L66-L67）；ZeRO-Offload 进一步用「单张 V100 训 13B」打开局面，见 [training.md:L77](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L77)。

**④ 可扩展性与 3D 并行。** 「3D 并行」= 数据并行 + 张量并行 + 流水线并行三者组合，官方文档说明它支撑过万亿参数模型，见 [training.md:L79-L88](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L79-L88)。这三个维度分别对应单元 5（ZeRO 数据并行）、单元 6（张量/序列并行、流水线并行）。

**⑤ 核心 API 清单。** 文档后半部分总结了 DeepSpeed 的核心 API，只有寥寥几个方法：`initialize`、`backward`、`step`、`add_config_arguments`、`load_checkpoint` / `store_checkpoint`，见 [training.md:L305-L314](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L305-L314)。这是单元 2 的预习提纲：整个训练引擎对用户暴露的入口就这么几个。

**⑥ 特性深读区（后半页）。** 从 [training.md:L233-L259](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L233-L259) 开始逐项解释 ZeRO 的子优化（优化器状态与梯度切分、激活切分、恒定缓冲区优化 CBO、连续内存优化 CMO）——这四个名词在单元 5 读 `stage_1_and_2.py` / `stage3.py` 时会一一对应到具体代码。ZeRO-Offload 的展开说明见 [training.md:L279-L283](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L279-L283)。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：training.md 中 ZeRO 的官方一句话定义是什么？它和数据并行的本质区别在哪里？

答案：ZeRO 与「在数据并行进程间复制内存状态」的基本数据并行不同，它把模型状态（model states）和梯度**切分（partition）**到各进程以节省内存（见 [training.md:L62-L65](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L62-L65)）。本质区别：复制 vs 切分——切分换来的是显存节省，付出的是用时需临时通信聚合。

**练习 2**：文档说 DeepSpeed 的核心 API「只有一把手能数得过来的几个方法」，请列举它们。

答案：`initialize`（初始化）、`backward` 和 `step`（训练）、`add_config_arguments`（参数解析）、`load_checkpoint` 和 `store_checkpoint`（检查点），见 [training.md:L305-L310](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L305-L310)。

**练习 3**：「3D 并行」中的三个维度是什么？ZeRO 在其中扮演哪个维度？

答案：数据并行、张量/模型并行、流水线并行（见 [training.md:L80-L82](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L80-L82)）。ZeRO 强化的是数据并行这一维（内存高效的数据并行），且可与另外两类并行组合。

### 4.3 版本与发布线

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

「这个仓库现在是哪个版本？」看似简单，但在 DeepSpeed 里版本信息有一条清晰的**传递链**：

```
version.txt（唯一事实来源，当前 0.19.9）
   ├─→ setup.py 打包时读取 → PyPI 发布的包版本
   └─→ (构建期写入) deepspeed/git_version_info.py
          └─→ deepspeed/__init__.py 导出 __version__ / __git_hash__ / __git_branch__
```

理解这条链的意义在于：**用户看到的 `deepspeed.__version__` 与仓库里的 `version.txt` 是同源的**；而且 DeepSpeed 还把 git 提交哈希打进包里，运行时日志会打印 version + git-hash + git-branch，这对你排查「线上到底跑的是哪份代码」极其有用（阅读源码时也能用它确认代码与讲义引用的 HEAD 一致）。

另一个要点是**发布节奏**：DeepSpeed 是「rolling master」模式——master 分支持续合入，定期打 tag 发 PyPI。所以 `git log` 里的最新提交就是最真实的项目动态，比新闻列表更细粒度。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

版本信息的生命周期：

1. 开发期：`version.txt` 由维护者更新，`0.19.9` 表示主版本 0、次版本 19、补丁版本 9。
2. 构建期：`setup.py` 读取 `version.txt`；如果设置了 `DS_BUILD_STRING` 环境变量则附加 `.devX` 后缀，否则把 git 哈希写入版本串，并生成 `deepspeed/git_version_info.py`。
3. 运行期：`import deepspeed` 时从 `git_version_info` 导入 version / git_hash / git_branch，暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__`、`deepspeed.__git_hash__`。
4. 日志期：每次 `initialize()` 都会打印 `DeepSpeed info: version=..., git-hash=..., git-branch=...`。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**① 唯一事实来源：version.txt。** 整个文件只有一行：

见 [version.txt:L1](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/version.txt#L1)——内容就是 `0.19.9`。这就是本手册撰写时仓库的版本号，也就是大纲中所说的 v0.19.9。

**② setup.py 消费版本号。** 安装脚本在打包时读取该文件：

见 [setup.py:L228-L229](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/setup.py#L228-L229)，注释明确写着「Parse the DeepSpeed version string from version.txt」。紧随其后（L231 起）的逻辑决定是否附加 `.dev` 后缀或 git 哈希。

**③ 包入口导出版本三元组与 git 信息。** `import deepspeed` 时：

见 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L70](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L70)，从 `git_version_info`（构建时生成）导入 version、git_hash、git_branch；随后在 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L75-L85](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L75-L85) 解析出主/次/补丁三元组并导出 `__version__`、`__git_hash__`、`__git_branch__`。同一个文件里，[deepspeed/__init__.py:L88](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L88) 附近的 `dist = None` 是个伏笔：分布式通信句柄被设计为延迟绑定（引擎初始化时才指向 `deepspeed.comm`），单元 3 会展开。

顺带一提，`deepspeed/__init__.py:498` 与 `721` 附近各有一行 `log_dist("DeepSpeed info: version={}, git-hash={}, git-branch={}"...)`——这就是运行时日志里版本行的出处。

#### 4.3.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：验证版本传递链的三环都指向同一个版本号。

**操作步骤**：

1. `cat version.txt` → 记下输出（预期 `0.19.9`）。
2. `grep -n "version.txt" setup.py` → 确认 setup.py 第 229 行在读取它。
3. 若本地已安装 deepspeed：`python -c "import deepspeed; print(deepspeed.__version__, deepspeed.__git_hash__)"` → 对比输出与第 1 步结果，并核对 `__git_hash__` 的前 9 位是否等于 `git rev-parse --short=9 HEAD`（本仓库 HEAD 为 `dc046b15d`）。
4. `pip index versions deepspeed 2>/dev/null || pip install deepspeed==` → 观察 PyPI 上可用的版本列表，看看 0.19.9 处在发布线的什么位置。

**需要观察的现象**：第 3 步中 `__version__` 与 `version.txt` 一致；若你是 `pip install deepspeed` 装的正式发行版，`__git_hash__` 是打包那次提交的哈希；若是源码 editable 安装（`pip install -e .`），哈希应与你本地 HEAD 一致。

**预期结果**：三个环节读出的版本号完全一致。第 3、4 步依赖本地 Python 环境，**待本地验证**。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：写一份 1 页的《DeepSpeed 活跃方向调研笔记》——用 git 历史与 README 新闻互相印证。**

一份开源项目的「自我介绍」（README News）和它的「实际行为」（git log）对照着读，是判断项目健康度和方向的最快方法。本实践把前面三个模块串起来。

**实践目标**：从真实提交记录中识别出 3 个正在积极演进的子系统，并与 README 的 Latest News 互相印证。

**操作步骤**：

1. 进入仓库根目录，执行：

   ```bash
   git log --oneline -20
   ```

2. 把输出按主题分组。分组线索：提交信息开头的方括号标签（`[Hybrid Engine]`、`[AutoEP]`、`[AffineIR]`、`[VocabTP]`）和前缀（`ZeRO-1/2:`、`ZeRO-3:`、`ci:`）。
3. 打开 [README.md:L27-L67](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L27-L67) 的 Latest News（含 More news），为每个分组找一条时间上最近的新闻佐证。
4. 用 `git log --oneline -20 -- deepspeed/runtime/zero/` 这样的路径过滤命令，分别统计各主题目录的提交热度。
5. 写成 1 页笔记，每个方向包含：方向名、证据提交（哈希 + 一句话）、README 佐证新闻（日期 + 标题）、一句话判断它解决的是显存墙 / 通信墙 / 吞吐中的哪一个。

**参考范例**（以下为撰写本讲时对 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的真实观察，可作为你的笔记样例）：

- **ZeRO 卸载与显存优化**：`dc046b15d`「ZeRO-1/2: preserve gradients across request boundaries until step」、`c6291b7e1`「ZeRO-3: copy offloaded master weights back to the device through pinned buffer」——佐证新闻：SuperOffload 获 ASPLOS 2026 提名（2026/03）、ZenFlow（2025/08）。主攻**显存墙**。
- **专家并行 AutoEP / AffineIR**：`66fef47b2`、`f81850499`、`12ffb9903`、`7501610ee` 四条 AutoEP/AffineIR 相关提交——佐证新闻：Ray x DeepSpeed Meetup 中提到的专家并行与 fused kernel 工作（2025/10）。主攻**吞吐与显存**。
- **混合引擎与张量并行**：`ab7fd98fa`「[Hybrid Engine] Enable graph capture ... on non-CUDA accelerators」、`1a956270f`「[VocabTP] vocab_parallel_ce support fused LM-head projection + loss」——佐证新闻：AutoTP（2025/03，More news）。主攻**推理/训练一体化与通信墙**。

**需要观察的现象**：git log 的主题分布与 README 新闻的优先级高度吻合——新闻是「宣言」，提交是「行动」；两者不一致的地方（例如某特性上了新闻但近期无提交）通常意味着该方向已进入稳定维护期。

**预期结果**：一份含 3 个方向、每个方向有提交证据 + 新闻佐证 + 一句话定位的 1 页笔记。完成后建议存档在 `DeepSpeed-tutorial/` 之外的自有笔记目录里，学习单元 5 和单元 6 时回头验证你的判断。

## 6. 本讲小结

- DeepSpeed 是面向超大模型训练与推理的**底层优化库**，三大痛点是**显存墙、通信墙、训练吞吐**；核心创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D 并行、Ulysses 序列并行与 DeepSpeed-MoE（[README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)）。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

下一讲（u1-l2「代码地图：仓库目录结构与模块导览」）将钻进 `deepspeed/` 主包，逐一认识 runtime、ops、module_inject、csrc 等目录的职责分工，并精读 `deepspeed/__init__.py` 的导出列表。在进入下一讲之前，建议你：

1. 把本讲的「文档小节 ↔ 源码目录」对照表再过一遍，下一讲会把每个目录展开讲。
2. 通读一遍 [README.md:L123-L169](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L123-L169) 的安装章节，留意「JIT 编译」与「预编译」两种算子构建方式的区别——这是 u1-l3 的主题。

# DeepSpeed 项目全景：大模型训练为什么需要它

> 本讲是整本学习手册的第一讲。你不写一行 DeepSpeed 代码，只需要建立三样东西：对项目定位的认知、对文档地图的熟悉、对版本机制的把握。它们是后续所有源码阅读的坐标系。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清楚 DeepSpeed 解决的三大核心痛点：**显存墙**（模型放不进显存）、**通信墙**（多卡之间数据搬运太慢）、**训练吞吐**（整体训练太慢）。
2. 列举 DeepSpeed 的代表性系统创新：**ZeRO**、**ZeRO-Infinity / ZeRO-Offload**、**3D-Parallelism**、**Ulysses 序列并行**、**DeepSpeed-MoE** 等。
3. 知道仓库当前版本（0.19.9）、文档入口（deepspeed.ai 与 `docs/` 目录），以及它与 HuggingFace Transformers / Accelerate / Lightning 等框架的集成关系。
4. 学会用 `git log` 观察一个开源项目「最近在忙什么」，把 README 的新闻列表和实际代码提交互相印证。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲几乎不需要分布式训练背景，但以下概念会反复出现，先用大白话解释：

- **参数量 Ψ（psi）**：模型里所有可训练权重标量的总数。一个 7B 模型有约 70 亿个参数。显存讨论中常用 Ψ 代指「参数个数」。
- **数据并行（Data Parallelism, DP）**：每张卡都持有**完整的**模型副本，各自吃不同批次的数据，反向传播后同步梯度。最易用，但每张卡都重复存一份模型状态——这就是显存浪费的根源。
- **显存墙（memory wall）**：以混合精度 + Adam 优化器为例，除了参数本身，还要存梯度和优化器状态（Adam 的一阶/二阶动量、fp32 主权重）。粗略估算，训练状态约占

  \[ 2\Psi(\text{fp16 参数}) + 2\Psi(\text{fp16 梯度}) + 12\Psi(\text{fp32 优化器状态}) = 16\Psi \text{ 字节} \]

  一个 7B 模型仅模型状态就需要约 112 GB，而单卡显存通常只有 40~96 GB——模型还没跑起来就「撞墙」了。
- **通信墙（communication wall）**：多卡训练要在卡间搬运梯度/参数。当通信时间接近甚至超过计算时间，加卡不再提速。
- **ZeRO（Zero Redundancy Optimizer）**：DeepSpeed 的招牌技术。核心想法一句话：数据并行下每张卡都存了**完整副本**，这是冗余的；ZeRO 把优化器状态、梯度、参数逐级**切分**到各卡上，用时再临时聚合，从而用「通信换显存」。细节在单元 5 展开，本讲只需记住它是 DeepSpeed 的立身之本。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲涉及的文件很少，都是「项目门面」级别的文件：

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | 项目第一入口：新闻、定位、集成生态、硬件支持表、安装方式、论文列表 |
| `docs/_pages/training.md` | 官网「训练总览」页面的源文件，相当于官方版能力矩阵与特性清单 |
| `version.txt` | 单行文件，记录当前版本号（0.19.9），是发布线的源头 |
| `setup.py` | 安装脚本，从这里消费 `version.txt` |
| `deepspeed/__init__.py` | 主包入口，把版本号暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__` |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 README 的能力矩阵

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

读一个大型开源项目的第一步不是看代码，而是读它的 README，并从中提炼出一张「能力矩阵」：**它解决什么问题、靠什么技术解决、和谁协作、支持什么硬件**。

DeepSpeed 的 README 把这些信息分散在几个板块里：

| README 板块 | 回答的问题 |
| --- | --- |
| Latest News（L27 起） | 项目最近在往哪个方向演进 |
| Extreme Speed and Scale（L71 起） | 项目一句话定位与核心创新点 |
| DeepSpeed Adoption（L79 起） | 哪些著名大模型用它训出来、与哪些框架集成 |
| Build Pipeline Status（L110 起） | 在哪些硬件平台上跑 CI（即官方背书的平台） |
| Installation / HW support（L123 起） | 怎么装、支持哪些加速器 |
| Publications（L223 起） | 每项技术对应的论文 |

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把 README 当地图来「测绘」的流程：

1. 先看定位句（Extreme Speed and Scale 段），抓住核心创新关键词。
2. 再看 Latest News，按时间倒序扫一遍，找出反复出现的主题（这些就是活跃战线）。
3. 然后看 Adoption 与集成表，确认生态位：它是「库」，被上层框架调用，而不是取代它们。
4. 最后看 Build Pipeline / HW support 表，确认硬件矩阵，这决定了后续读源码时会遇到的多后端抽象（单元 3 会讲）。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① 一句话定位与五大创新点。** README 在标题段直接列出了 DeepSpeed 的系统创新清单：

> 这些创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D-Parallelism、Ulysses Sequence Parallelism、DeepSpeed-MoE 等。

见 [README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)。这段话就是整本学习手册的「课程大纲」：单元 5 讲 ZeRO 系列，单元 6 讲 3D 并行 / Ulysses / MoE。README 还点出 DeepSpeed 训练过 MT-530B、BLOOM 等当时的最大模型，见 [README.md:L84-L95](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L84-L95)。

**② Latest News：项目的活跃战线。** 新闻列表从 2026/05 一直排到 2025/06，见 [README.md:L27-L51](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L27-L51)。几个值得记住的条目：

- Muon 优化器支持与 ZeRO-3 的 SDMA 卸载（2026/05，L29-L31）；
- SuperOffload 获 ASPLOS 2026 最佳论文提名（2026/03，L35）；
- Core API 更新：PyTorch 风格 backward 与低精度主权重（2025/12，L37）；
- ZenFlow 无停顿卸载引擎（2025/08，L47）。

折叠区「More news」里还有三条：DeepCompile（编译优化）、AutoTP（自动张量并行）、Ulysses-Offload（长上下文），见 [README.md:L55-L67](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L55-L67)。这些名字后续单元都会对应到具体源码目录（如 `deepspeed/compile/`、`deepspeed/module_inject/auto_tp.py`、`deepspeed/runtime/zenflow/`）。

**③ 集成生态：DeepSpeed 是「被集成」的库。** README 用一张表列出与主流框架的集成文档，见 [README.md:L97-L106](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L97-L106)：

- HuggingFace **Transformers**（L101）——最常见用法：`TrainingArguments` 里打开 `deepspeed` 即可；
- HuggingFace **Accelerate**（L102）；
- PyTorch **Lightning**、**MosaicML**、**Determined**、**MMEngine**（L103-L106）。

这说明 DeepSpeed 的生态位是**底层训练加速库**：用户通常不直接面对它，而是通过这些上层框架间接使用。但要看懂它为什么快、为什么省显存，必须回到源码——这正是本手册的目的。

**④ 硬件能力矩阵。** CI 表见 [README.md:L110-L121](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L110-L121)：NVIDIA、AMD、CPU、Intel Gaudi（hpu）、Intel XPU、华为昇腾 NPU 都有独立 CI。社区贡献的硬件表见 [README.md:L141-L151](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L141-L151)，列出各加速器的短名（`npu`、`hpu`、`cpu`、`xpu`、`sdaa`、`klxpu`）。这张表解释了为什么源码里会有一整套「加速器抽象层」（`deepspeed/accelerator/`，单元 3 精读）：一套代码要同时跑在这么多硬件上。

**⑤ 论文索引。** [README.md:L223-L262](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L223-L262) 的 Publications 列表是按技术查论文的入口：ZeRO 原论文（L224）、ZeRO-Infinity（L229）、DeepSpeed-MoE（L233）、ZeRO++（L245）、ZenFlow（L260）、SuperOffload（L262）等。读源码卡住时，回这里找对应论文往往能豁然开朗。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：亲手从 README 提炼出一张属于自己的能力矩阵表。

**操作步骤**：

1. 打开仓库根目录的 `README.md`（本讲用 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的版本）。
2. 用编辑器搜索以下小标题并记下其起始行号：`Latest News`、`Extreme Speed`、`DeepSpeed Adoption`、`Build Pipeline Status`、`Installation`、`Contributed HW support`、`Publications`。
3. 为每个板块用一句话总结它回答的问题，填进 4.1.1 的表格里替换掉我们的答案。
4. 统计 Latest News 中 2025-2026 年条目里出现次数最多的技术关键词（提示：offload/ZenFlow/SuperOffload 相关条目出现了 4 次以上）。

**需要观察的现象**：你会发现 README 的新闻列表不是随机罗列——offload（卸载）方向（ZeRO-Offload → ZeRO-Infinity → ZenFlow → SuperOffload）和并行方向（3D → AutoTP → AutoEP）各自成线，每条线都能在 Publications 里找到对应论文、在源码目录里找到对应模块。

**预期结果**：得到一张 7 行左右的能力矩阵表，并且能回答「DeepSpeed 最近一年最重要的三个新方向是什么」。如果答案里包含「卸载引擎（ZenFlow/SuperOffload）」「自动并行注入（AutoTP/AutoEP）」「编译优化（DeepCompile）」之一，说明读对了。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：README 说 DeepSpeed 的核心创新包括哪五项？分别对应手册的哪个单元？

答案：ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D-Parallelism、Ulysses 序列并行、DeepSpeed-MoE（见 [README.md:L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L73)）。对应关系：ZeRO → 单元 5；3D 并行与 Ulysses → 单元 6；MoE → 单元 6；ZeRO-Infinity（NVMe 交换）→ 单元 5 第 7 讲。

**练习 2**：如果你在用 HuggingFace Transformers 训练模型，README 里哪个链接告诉你如何配合 DeepSpeed 使用？

答案：集成表第一行的 [Transformers with DeepSpeed](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/deepspeed) 文档链接，见 [README.md:L101](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L101)。

**练习 3**：README 的 CI 表为什么要为 AMD、CPU、Gaudi、XPU、昇腾分别设置流水线？这对源码结构有什么暗示？

答案：因为 DeepSpeed 明确支持多硬件平台（每个平台一个 CI workflow 保证不回归），见 [README.md:L110-L121](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L110-L121)。源码结构上的暗示是：一定存在一层设备无关抽象把硬件差异挡住——即 `deepspeed/accelerator/`（单元 3 会精读），项目规则也禁止直接 `import torch.distributed` 而要求走统一通信层。

### 4.2 训练文档结构

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`docs/` 目录是 DeepSpeed 官网（deepspeed.ai）的源文件，用 Jekyll 构建。其中 `docs/_pages/training.md` 是官网「Training Overview and Features」页面的源文件——可以把它理解为**官方版能力矩阵**：README 用一段话告诉你「有什么」，training.md 用整篇文档告诉你「每项特性具体是什么、怎么开」。

这个文件有个有趣的细节：它实际上包含**两个 Jekyll 页面**（两段 front matter），前半部分是 `/training/`（训练总览），后半部分是 `/features/`（特性详解）。读它时要意识到自己在「两页文档」之间穿越。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

training.md 的叙事结构本身就是一条问题-方案链，推荐按这个顺序读：

```
训练大模型难（Overview, L9-17）
  ├─ 要自己搭分布式/混合精度/梯度累积/检查点 → DeepSpeed API 轻量包装 PyTorch（L19-27）
  ├─ 太慢 → Speed：BERT-large 44 分钟、GPT-2 3.75x（L29-52）
  ├─ 显存不够 → Memory efficiency：ZeRO、ZeRO-Offload（L56-77）
  ├─ 规模上天 → Scalability：3D 并行、万亿参数（L79-96）
  ├─ 网络带宽差 → Communication efficiency：流水线并行降通信（L98-100）
  ├─ 数据太多 → Data efficiency：课程学习、token dropping（L102-103）
  ├─ 收敛太慢 → LAMB 等大 batch 优化器（L105-111）
  └─ 都想要但怕难用 → Good usability：几行代码接入（L114-115）
```

前半部分以「叙事」收尾于一张特性清单（L118-163）；后半部分（L165 起）逐项展开每个特性的细节与配置片段。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① 问题描述：为什么需要 DeepSpeed。** 文档开篇直接点出双重痛点——既要搭好分布式/混合精度这些「样板代码」，又可能得不到理想的性能；大模型在纯数据并行下显存直接爆掉，而模型并行又难用：

见 [training.md:L9-L17](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L9-L17)。这句「a large model easily runs out of memory with pure data parallelism」就是第 2 节讲的显存墙的官方表述。

**② 产品哲学：轻量包装，不另起炉灶。** DeepSpeed API 被定位为「PyTorch 之上的轻量包装」——你仍用 PyTorch 的一切，DeepSpeed 接管分布式训练、混合精度、梯度累积、检查点这些样板技术，见 [training.md:L19-L27](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L19-L27)。这解释了为什么手册单元 2 讲 `initialize()` 时你会看到：模型、优化器、数据加载器都还是 PyTorch 对象，DeepSpeed 只是「包」了一层引擎。

### 4.3 版本与发布线

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

「这个仓库现在是哪个版本？」看似简单，但在 DeepSpeed 里版本信息有一条清晰的**传递链**：

```
version.txt（唯一事实来源，当前 0.19.9）
   ├─→ setup.py 打包时读取 → PyPI 发布的包版本
   └─→ (构建期写入) deepspeed/git_version_info.py
          └─→ deepspeed/__init__.py 导出 __version__ / __git_hash__ / __git_branch__
```

理解这条链的意义在于：**用户看到的 `deepspeed.__version__` 与仓库里的 `version.txt` 是同源的**；而且 DeepSpeed 还把 git 提交哈希打进包里，运行时日志会打印 version + git-hash + git-branch，这对你排查「线上到底跑的是哪份代码」极其有用（阅读源码时也能用它确认代码与讲义引用的 HEAD 一致）。

另一个要点是**发布节奏**：DeepSpeed 是「rolling master」模式——master 分支持续合入，定期打 tag 发 PyPI。所以 `git log` 里的最新提交就是最真实的项目动态，比新闻列表更细粒度。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

版本信息的生命周期：

1. 开发期：`version.txt` 由维护者更新，`0.19.9` 表示主版本 0、次版本 19、补丁版本 9。
2. 构建期：`setup.py` 读取 `version.txt`；如果设置了 `DS_BUILD_STRING` 环境变量则附加 `.devX` 后缀，否则把 git 哈希写入版本串，并生成 `deepspeed/git_version_info.py`。
3. 运行期：`import deepspeed` 时从 `git_version_info` 导入 version / git_hash / git_branch，暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__`、`deepspeed.__git_hash__`。
4. 日志期：每次 `initialize()` 都会打印 `DeepSpeed info: version=..., git-hash=..., git-branch=...`。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：写一份 1 页的《DeepSpeed 活跃方向调研笔记》——用 git 历史与 README 新闻互相印证。**

一份开源项目的「自我介绍」（README News）和它的「实际行为」（git log）对照着读，是判断项目健康度和方向的最快方法。本实践把前面三个模块串起来。

**实践目标**：从真实提交记录中识别出 3 个正在积极演进的子系统，并与 README 的 Latest News 互相印证。

**操作步骤**：

1. 进入仓库根目录，执行：

   ```bash
   git log --oneline -20
   ```

2. 把输出按主题分组。分组线索：提交信息开头的方括号标签（`[Hybrid Engine]`、`[AutoEP]`、`[AffineIR]`、`[VocabTP]`）和前缀（`ZeRO-1/2:`、`ZeRO-3:`、`ci:`）。

4. 用 `git log --oneline -20 -- deepspeed/runtime/zero/` 这样的路径过滤命令，分别统计各主题目录的提交热度。
5. 写成 1 页笔记，每个方向包含：方向名、证据提交（哈希 + 一句话）、README 佐证新闻（日期 + 标题）、一句话判断它解决的是显存墙 / 通信墙 / 吞吐中的哪一个。

**参考范例**（以下为撰写本讲时对 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的真实观察，可作为你的笔记样例）：

- **ZeRO 卸载与显存优化**：`dc046b15d`「ZeRO-1/2: preserve gradients across request boundaries until step」、`c6291b7e1`「ZeRO-3: copy offloaded master weights back to the device through pinned buffer」——佐证新闻：SuperOffload 获 ASPLOS 2026 提名（2026/03）、ZenFlow（2025/08）。主攻**显存墙**。

- **混合引擎与张量并行**：`ab7fd98fa`「[Hybrid Engine] Enable graph capture ... on non-CUDA accelerators」、`1a956270f`「[VocabTP] vocab_parallel_ce support fused LM-head projection + loss」——佐证新闻：AutoTP（2025/03，More news）。主攻**推理/训练一体化与通信墙**。

**需要观察的现象**：git log 的主题分布与 README 新闻的优先级高度吻合——新闻是「宣言」，提交是「行动」；两者不一致的地方（例如某特性上了新闻但近期无提交）通常意味着该方向已进入稳定维护期。

**预期结果**：一份含 3 个方向、每个方向有提交证据 + 新闻佐证 + 一句话定位的 1 页笔记。完成后建议存档在 `DeepSpeed-tutorial/` 之外的自有笔记目录里，学习单元 5 和单元 6 时回头验证你的判断。

## 6. 本讲小结

- DeepSpeed 是面向超大模型训练与推理的**底层优化库**，三大痛点是**显存墙、通信墙、训练吞吐**；核心创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D 并行、Ulysses 序列并行与 DeepSpeed-MoE（[README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)）。
- README 的板块结构本身就是一张能力矩阵：News 看方向、Adoption 看生态（Transformers/Accelerate/Lightning 都在集成它）、CI 与 HW 表看硬件版图（NVIDIA/AMD/CPU/Gaudi/XPU/昇腾等）。
- `docs/_pages/training.md` 是官方能力矩阵的展开版：按「难 → 快 → 省 → 大 → 通 → 效 → 易」的问题链组织；其中 ZeRO 的定义（切分而非复制）与核心 API 清单（`initialize`/`backward`/`step`/checkpoint）是单元 2 的直接预习材料。
- 版本传递链：`version.txt`（0.19.9）→ `setup.py` 打包 → `deepspeed.__version__` / `__git_hash__`；运行时日志会打印 version + git-hash + git-branch，用于精确定位代码版本。
- 阅读 »README News + git log« 双轨对照是判断开源项目活跃方向的标准手法；当前最活跃的三条线是 ZeRO 卸载（ZenFlow/SuperOffload 系）、专家并行（AutoEP/AffineIR）、混合引擎/张量并行。
